model.rationale: Houchin pairs a fifteen-point Republican district lean with a roughly ten-to-one fundraising advantage, and prediction markets price her win odds above ninety percent. With no polls or expert ratings signaling vulnerability and the challenger lacking resources, the race stays firmly in the Safe Republican column.

overview:
Indiana's 9th District, covering the state's southern counties, leans Republican by about fifteen points. Republican Erin Houchin runs for re-election against Democrat Brad Meyer, with Libertarian Tonya Hudson also on the ballot. Houchin has raised about $1.9 million and holds more than $1.1 million on hand, while Meyer has raised roughly $105,000 with under $20,000 available. No outside groups have reported spending on either side.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the contest, so the picture rests on district fundamentals and money. Prediction markets give Houchin about a 93 percent chance of winning, implying a comfortable double-digit margin. A favorable national climate for Democrats could trim the gap somewhat, but the combination of a red-leaning electorate, an entrenched incumbent, and a lopsided financial edge makes an upset highly unlikely.
